name: Paetongtarn Shinawatra
summary: Paetongtarn combined economic stimulus, social provision and investment promotion with support for Thailand’s constitutional monarchy. Her government implemented marriage equality and restricted recreational cannabis; her promises of political liberalization were accompanied by continued royal-insult prosecutions.

sources.title: Policy Statement delivered to the National Assembly, September 12, 2024
sources.author: Paetongtarn Shinawatra / Royal Thai Government
sources.usedFor: Government program, substantive speech pages 1–16; constitutional appendix distinguished from her own commitments.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Her government increased minimum wages, reaching 400 baht in Bangkok and specified industries, with lower provincial rates retained.

cut-welfare.rationale: Commits to expanded welfare and living-cost support.

legalize-drugs.rationale: She instructed her cabinet to restrict cannabis to medical use rather than permit recreational sales.

decide-locally.rationale: Promises decentralization to local governments and communities.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Her government implemented and publicly celebrated marriage equality in January 2025.

more-religion-public.rationale: Supports religious institutions to promote public morality.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Promotes traditional Thai arts and cultural production.

free-trade.rationale: She promoted the Thailand–EFTA agreement and further trade negotiations as opportunities for economic development.

nation-first.rationale: Places national interests at diplomacy’s core.

open-borders.rationale: She defended deportation of forty Uyghurs, arguing confirmed nationality required return despite their long detention and refugee claims.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Commits to carbon neutrality and industrial decarbonization.

expand-nuclear.rationale: She witnessed her government’s agreement with China to prepare for small modular reactors, short of a construction commitment.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Directs investment toward strategic manufacturing and infrastructure.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Explicitly commits to preserving constitutional monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: She calls for a more democratic country and rejects the unelected senate’s power over government formation.

conscription.rationale: Promises transition to voluntary military service.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Combines stimulus borrowing with strict fiscal-discipline commitments.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Explicitly includes stateless persons in welfare access.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Supports new energy exploration, including Cambodian offshore claims.

consent-of-governed.rationale: She objects that military-appointed senators lack a popular mandate and should not override voters.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Prioritizes vulnerable groups in economic stimulus.

central-bank-independence.rationale: She explicitly called central-bank independence an obstacle to addressing economic problems.

delink-world-market.rationale: Her international investment and trade promotion pursues deeper integration rather than economic disengagement.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Promises protection against workplace discrimination against women.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: She explicitly invited foreign investment to advance Thailand’s economy.

military-guardian-role.rationale: She rejects military coups as a way to decide who governs.

suppress-opposition.rationale: She promised bail and discussion of misuse of royal-insult charges, but retained the law and prosecutions continued under her government.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Supports public participation in local decision-making.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Explicitly promises gender equality within families.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Her cabinet approved a carbon-price component in fuel excise, alongside other environmental measures.

notes: No inferred answers. All 490 statements and remaining nulls reviewed. The full English policy PDF was opened through the web reader; its direct download returned an access page. The full Thai transcription was downloaded as an additional searchable text. Political-rights evidence is mixed: opposition prosecutions continued, but independent military and judicial decisions are not automatically treated as her personal instructions. Unused public-land distribution is not confiscation of private estates. LGBT family rights do not alone establish legal gender-marker recognition. Nuclear cooperation is preparatory. Her election after her father does not establish hereditary succession as a principle. No position is imputed from relatives or party membership.
